issues.failure_explanation: The cross terms contain a coefficient, an L^p function, and an L^2 gradient. Hölder therefore requires 1/r + 1/p + 1/2 ≤ 1, which is not supplied by r=p/2 for the full stated range. For example, at p=4 in dimension three, an L^2 coefficient behaving as |x|^(-5/4) and H_0^1 test functions behaving as |x|^(-2/5) near an interior point produce a nonintegrable cross term. Thus the displayed assumptions do not suffice for the asserted bounded derivative form.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Require both cross coefficients to belong to L^{2p/(p-2)}, with L^infinity at p=2, or restrict this particular sufficient-condition statement to p≥6.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed sufficient conditions for the quasilinear linearisation fail for permitted choices of p, including p=4.
issues.title: Insufficient integrability exponents for quasilinear cross terms
issues.why_classification: This is a local Hölder-exponent repair; it requires no new verification argument and leaves the semilinear results unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: The paper assumes only f∈H^{-1}, but the estimator and reconstruction require volume densities with element means and L^2 residual norms. For example, f=∂_1 1_E for an interior Lipschitz set E belongs to H^{-1}, since its action is bounded by |E|^(1/2)||∇v||, but it has no L^2 volume density. Subtracting an H(div) divergence does not remove this singular part. Even for function-valued loads, the stated lower-order coefficient assumptions do not ensure s_h∈L^2. The theorem omits the regularity needed to define its certified quantity.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Explicitly restrict these constructions to s_h∈L^2 and, for the adjoint application, s_h^ast∈L^2. Retaining general H^{-1} data would additionally require a certified dual-norm data-approximation error term.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised realisation of (C1), its cell-mean reconstruction, and the analogous adjoint application are not supplied for the full stated data class.
issues.title: Residual certification is undefined for the admitted H^{-1} data
issues.why_classification: The direct repair genuinely narrows the stated V* data scope, although it preserves a comparable residual-certification method for L^2 data.

issues.failure_explanation: In dimensions two and three, H_0^1 with the stated uniformly elliptic energy norm does not embed into L^infinity. Unbounded H_0^1 functions can be scaled into arbitrarily small positive energy balls, so neither the asserted finite C_infinity nor a uniform M_infinity on such a ball exists. The conditional calculation therefore provides no actual instance of the claimed quasilinear verification in the paper's functional setting.

issues.title: Quasilinear example assumes an impossible energy-to-L-infinity embedding
issues.why_classification: The required assumptions cannot hold in any positive verification ball. Retaining the advertised example requires new functional-space proof architecture; otherwise that regime must be abandoned.

Let $\sigma_h^{\ast}\in H(\div;\Omega)$ be any flux satisfying the (adjoint) divergence target $\div\sigma_h^{\ast}=r_h^{\ast}$ elementwise.

issues.failure_explanation: With the stated source and divergence target, G has diffusion field -A∇z_h, so the residual theorem requires the mismatch σ_h^ast+A∇z_h, not σ_h^ast-A∇z_h. For a counterexample, take A=I, c'=0, ψ=1, let z_h solve Δz_h=1 with zero boundary data, and choose σ_h^ast=∇z_h. The printed mismatch and oscillation both vanish, whereas G(v)=2∫Ωv is nonzero.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Apply the residual theorem to -G with flux -σ_h^ast, obtaining ||σ_h^ast+A∇z_h|| in the mismatch term, and reevaluate the affected output budgets.
issues.overall_effect: The proposed computable substitute for the adjoint residual norm can underestimate it, so output budgets using that substitute are not justified. The enclosure theorem using the true residual norm remains valid.
issues.title: Adjoint residual majorant uses the wrong flux sign
issues.why_classification: A sign-consistent application of the existing theorem repairs the estimate using the same reconstructed flux, without a new analytic ingredient or a weaker output guarantee.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: All computations in Section~9 were performed with an implementation based on FEniCSx (dolfinx) and PETSc, using IEEE double precision.

issues.failure_explanation: Even with exact source averages, normal continuity of the Marini fields requires the auxiliary CR equations to hold exactly. For an inexact CR solution, the proof identifies the integrated normal jump on a face with the unsatisfied CR equation tested by that face's basis function. Thus the locally reconstructed field need not belong to H(div). Outward rounding of the final mismatch and oscillation scalars does not account for the omitted face-jump functional or establish exact conformity.

failure_location.quote: If fully rigorous guarantees against rounding are required, one may apply outward rounding/interval arithmetic only in this final scalar post-processing step, while keeping the primal/adjoint solves unchanged.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Validate or enclose the auxiliary CR solution, or enforce the RT continuity constraints with certified correction/defect bounds, before evaluating the final scalar majorant. The primal and adjoint approximations may still remain unverified.
issues.overall_effect: The stated scalar-only upgrade to full rounding rigour is unsupported for the implemented reconstruction. The exact-arithmetic reconstruction lemma itself remains valid.
issues.title: Scalar outward rounding does not validate the auxiliary CR flux
issues.why_classification: A contained auxiliary-solve validation or flux-defect argument is needed; merely changing scalar rounding is insufficient, but the overall certification architecture can be retained.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: If the quick test fails, bracket an admissible radius by testing a geometric sequence (e.g.,  $\rho_j=2^{-j}\rho_0$) until $p(\rho_j)\le 0$ and $q(\rho_j)<1$ hold.

issues.failure_explanation: For η>0 and L(ρ)>0, every 0<ρ≤η has p(ρ)=η−ρ+L(ρ)ρ²/(2α)>0. After rejecting 2η, the algorithm tests only η, η/2, and smaller values, so it can never enter its bisection phase. This is not merely an empty-admissible-set case: with α=1, η=1/2, and L(ρ)=ρ, the initial radius 1 fails q<1, while ρ=4/5 has p=-11/250 and q=16/25. The advertised fallback nevertheless always returns fail.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: For the affine model, locate the minimum of the convex polynomial p, test a feasible point there, and then form a genuine admissible/inadmissible upper bracket before bisection.
issues.overall_effect: The supposed bracketing–bisection fallback provides no capability beyond the initial quick test and misses certifiable affine-model inputs.
issues.title: Halving from 2η makes fallback bracketing unreachable
issues.why_classification: A different contained radius-search construction is required. Convexity supports such a repair without changing the NK framework or its guarantees.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Then, the admissible set $\mathcal {AD}$ is either empty or an interval of the form

issues.failure_explanation: Intersecting a closed p-sublevel interval with an open q-interval does not necessarily remove the p-interval's upper endpoint. For α=L1=1, L0=0, and η=sqrt(8/27), p has its unique zero at ρ0=sqrt(2/3), with q(ρ0)=2/3; hence AD={ρ0}, not a half-open interval. Nondegenerate closed admissible intervals also occur when the upper p-root precedes q=1. At the other endpoint, η=0 with the same α and L gives AD=(0,1), contradicting the claimed strictly positive, included lower endpoint.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Retain the actual intersection with ρ>0 and distinguish closed upper endpoints, open upper endpoints, singletons, and the open zero lower endpoint. Use weak upper-threshold bracket inequalities where necessary.
issues.overall_effect: The asserted exact topology and the claim that admissibility always fails at the upper threshold are false. Convexity and the conditional bisection guarantee still survive.
issues.title: Incorrect endpoint structure of the admissible-radius set
issues.why_classification: Routine endpoint case analysis preserves the interval property, the NK tests, and the bisection error bound without new proof architecture.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \State \Comment{Bisection to approximate the maximal admissible radius}

issues.failure_explanation: Opposite signs identify some zero of p, not necessarily the upper admissibility threshold. For α=1, L(ρ)=ρ, and η=0.1, the lower p-root is approximately 0.10051, while the upper admissibility threshold is 1, imposed by q<1. Values immediately to either side of the lower root have opposite p-signs although the upper threshold is far away. Thus the stated inference fails even with exact arithmetic.

failure_location.quote: Observing opposite signs at $(1-\delta)\rho$ and $(1+\delta)\rho$ indicates that the computed $\rho$ lies close to a sign change of $p$ and that the bisection has localised the threshold to within a relative tolerance $\delta$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use the final bisection bracket and its proved width bound, or require the lower test point to be admissible and the upper test point to be inadmissible, checking q as well as p.
issues.overall_effect: The optional diagnostic can falsely suggest that the maximal admissible radius has been localized; it does not invalidate separately checked NK admissibility.
issues.title: The optional sign test does not locate the upper admissibility threshold
issues.why_classification: The existing bracket guarantee supplies a short local replacement, with no change to the existence or output certificates.
